# Free Lunch Lab

> Free Lunch Lab ("There is such a thing as a free lunch.") is a curated directory of apps and projects that pay you a basic income or rewards just for existing: crypto UBI, passive apps, cashback and more. Every entry links to its official source and has a "last checked" month, and the risks and cautions are listed next to the rewards. The site is available in 7 languages (en, ja, zh, hi, es, de, ar).

- Referral links: some sign-up links are the maintainer's referral links. They are marked in the data (`referral` in services.json); official URLs are always given too.
- License: content is CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), referral links excluded.
- Data last checked: 2026-11
- Full text: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/llms-full.txt

## Data

- [services.json](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services.json): all visible services as JSON, with descriptions in every language, region, invite-only flag, verification, trust check and referral info
- [graveyard.json](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard.json): ended basic-income-style programs, each with a source
- [open-source.json](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/open-source.json): open-source code projects related to basic income, with license, language, stars, last commit and dormant flag
- [open-data.json](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/open-data.json): open datasets and replication packages from basic income experiments, with archive, access level and license
- [RSS feed (en)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/feed.xml): update log in English
- [RSS feed (ja)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/ja/feed.xml): update log in 日本語
- [RSS feed (zh)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/zh/feed.xml): update log in 中文
- [RSS feed (hi)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/hi/feed.xml): update log in हिन्दी
- [RSS feed (es)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/es/feed.xml): update log in Español
- [RSS feed (de)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/de/feed.xml): update log in Deutsch
- [RSS feed (ar)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/ar/feed.xml): update log in العربية

## Services

- [GoodDollar](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/gooddollar/): G$ tokens every day. A nonprofit UBI protocol (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: Face scan / liveness)
- [Circles (Gnosis App)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/circles/): 1 CRC per hour (24 per day). A Gnosis project where every person issues their own currency (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; invite only; verification: Web of trust / invites)
- [ME Pass](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/mepass/): MEC tokens every day. Meta Earth's wallet app (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: ID document KYC)
- [BioMatrix](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/biomatrix/): PoY tokens every month. A UBI token that promises monthly payouts for 60 years (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: not specified)
- [Hapitas](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/hapitas/): Up to 2,300 points. October 2026 offer (1 point = ¥1) (Cashback sites; Japan only; verification: No verification)
- [Mercari](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/mercari/): ¥500 in points (can be auto-converted into Bitcoin and more). Mercari’s friend invite for its flea-market app (Cashback sites; Japan only; verification: Phone number, ID document KYC (optional))
- [WAVEE](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/wavee/): A matching reward each time you land a job. Invite-only job matching (Job matching; available in Japan and worldwide; invite only; verification: No verification)
- [Trima](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/trima/): 5,000 miles + miles for moving and walking. An app that earns miles just by carrying your phone as you travel and walk (Passive apps; Japan only; verification: No verification)
- [Sweatcoin](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/sweatcoin/): 0.95 coins per 1,000 steps. Carry your phone and your steps turn into coins automatically (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Grass](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/grass/): Points (later GRASS tokens). A DePIN that rents out your unused bandwidth for AI web scraping (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Honeygain](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/honeygain/): Cash for the traffic you share. The best-known bandwidth-sharing app: it rents your unused connection to businesses for web data collection (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Pawns.app](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/pawns/): Cash for the traffic you share. IPRoyal’s bandwidth-sharing app (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Pi Network](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/pinetwork/): PI every day. Tap a button in the app once every 24 hours to earn PI (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; invite only; verification: ID document KYC)
- [Delta Kim](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/deltakim/): KIM every day. A crypto app similar to Pi Network where you “mine” daily on your phone (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [InterLink](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/interlink/): ITLG tokens every day. A project that distributes ITLG tokens to people who have verified they are real humans through face verification (Human Nodes) (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: Face scan / liveness)
- [Mein Grundeinkommen](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/meingrundeinkommen/): €1,000 a month for a year if you win. A free lottery run by a nonprofit association in Berlin and funded by crowdfunding donations (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification, ID document KYC (optional))
- [UBI4ALL](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/ubi4all/): €9,600 if you win (in Japan: €800 a month for a year). A free raffle run by a German non-profit (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification, ID document KYC (optional))
- [Ğ1 (June)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/g1/): Ğ1 every day once you are a member (Universal Dividend). A libre currency based on the Relative Theory of Money (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; invite only; verification: Web of trust / invites)
- [Palai](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/palai/): Palai (¶) basic income every day. A currency that pays everyone a daily basic income just for being human (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: Phone number)
- [Dotare](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/dotare/): 10 ADA a month for a year if you are chosen (2027 cycle). A global basic income fund on Cardano (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: not specified)
- [ORO (World App)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/oro/): ORO tokens every day. A mini app inside World App that lets you claim the World Chain token ORO once a day (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: World ID (Orb))
- [AXO (World App)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/axo/): AXO tokens every day. A mini app inside World App: tap once a day to claim the World Chain token AXO (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: World ID (Orb))
- [AI-DAC (World App)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/aidac/): UBI in DAC tokens. A mini app inside World App that calls itself an “AI-powered universal basic income platform” (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: World ID (Orb))
- [Ubiquitus](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/ubiquitus/): A small equal cash share on the 1st of each month (Venmo). A US social experiment in a “basic income anyone can join” (Passive apps; US residents only, not available from Japan; verification: not specified)
- [Gradido](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/gradido/): 20 GDD per hour of common-good work (up to 1,000 GDD a month). A currency system that calls itself a “natural economy” (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [WowApp](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/wowapp/): Small rewards for daily use, games, shopping and more. A chat and calling app combined with a rewards system (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Humad (World App)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/humad/): Points for tapping ads and answering questions (gift cards from 1,500 pt = ¥150). A mini app inside World App (Cashback sites; Japan only; verification: World ID (Orb))
- [Billions](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/billions/): Power points (for verifying, referring friends and taking part). A digital ID app that proves you are a real human with your phone and ID (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: Face scan / liveness, NFC passport)
- [Idena (iDNA)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/idena/): iDNA (mining rewards while your node runs, plus validation rewards). A Proof-of-Person blockchain that proves you are human on a “one person, one vote” basis (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; invite only; verification: Validation ceremony, Web of trust / invites)
- [RewardMe](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/rewardme/): Up to 5% cashback found in your email receipts (Reward Dollars / MDT crypto). Link your email and it finds purchases at Amazon, Uber and other partner stores from receipt emails, earning up to 5% back (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification, World ID (Orb) (optional))
- [FheID (Privasea)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/fheid/): Airdrops and rewards for proving you are human (e.g. campaign “stars”). An app that scans your face with your phone camera to prove you are a real human (Crypto basic income; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: Face scan / liveness)
- [JrKripto (JR)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/jrkripto/): JR points every day (50 JR sign-up bonus). The mobile app of JrKripto, a Turkish crypto news, analysis and price-tracking site whose founder also runs the stock site JrHisse (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Mining Machine ($ORE)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/miningmachine/): $ORE mining balance (free 24-hour sessions). A site where a “mining machine” in your browser builds up a $ORE balance (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [KABU&](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/kabuand/): Share vouchers based on what you pay for electricity, gas, mobile and more (used to apply for unlisted shares). A service from Kabu & Peace Inc., led by Yusaku Maezawa (Cashback sites; Japan only; verification: ID document KYC)
- [Life AI Testnet](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/lifeai/): Testnet points (daily USDT draws; token and NFT rewards for top players). The testnet of Life AI, a healthcare AI project (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Refrax ($REFRAX)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/refrax/): Pending $REFRAX points (no token yet). Season 0 quests from Refrax, a project presenting itself as decentralized storage on Solana (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Sible Network ($SIB)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/siblenetwork/): SIBLE ($SIB) mining balance (not tradable). A Pi Network-style “AI mining” app where you tap to start mining sessions (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: not specified)
- [Perceptron Network (formerly BlockMesh)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/perceptron/): Points (no PERC token yet). A decentralized network that gathers AI training data (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)
- [Brave Rewards (Brave browser)](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/braverewards/): BAT (Basic Attention Token). Opt in to privacy-preserving Brave Ads in the Brave browser to earn BAT (Passive apps; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: ID document KYC)
- [AIBTC](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/services/aibtc/): sBTC bounties (pegged 1:1 to bitcoin). A network where AI agents, run by humans, hold Bitcoin and Stacks wallets and earn sBTC (For AI agents; available in Japan and worldwide; verification: No verification)

## Guides

- [What can you do with World ID? Apps that use Orb verification](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/world-id/): services that use World ID (Orb)
- [Apps that verify you with a face scan](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/face/): services that use Face scan / liveness
- [Apps that require ID document KYC](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/kyc-id/): services that use ID document KYC
- [Apps that verify you by phone number](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/phone/): services that use Phone number
- [Apps you join through invites or a web of trust](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/web-of-trust/): services that use Web of trust / invites
- [Apps that need no identity verification](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/verify/none/): services that use No verification
- [Basic income organizations & projects](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/organizations/): A curated list of organizations and projects around the world and in Japan that advocate, research or practise basic income (UBI), grouped by type. Checked in October 2026.
- [Basic income experiments: a timeline](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/timeline/): A timeline of basic income experiments and schemes, from Mincome and Alaska’s dividend to Namibia, Finland, Stockton, OpenResearch and Germany’s pilot, with who ran them, what was paid, results and sources.
- [The Free Lunch Graveyard](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/graveyard/): Services and programmes that once paid out money or points and have ended, such as World’s WLD airdrop and Miles, with end dates, reasons and sources.
- [Open-source basic income projects](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/open-source/): A curated list of open-source code projects behind basic income: UBI protocols, wallets, proof of personhood and policy simulators, with license, stars and last commit date.
- [A badge for listed projects](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/badge/): A small “Listed on Free Lunch Lab” badge for projects listed on this site, with ready-to-copy Markdown and HTML for every service, open-source project and organization. Image: https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/badge/listed.svg. Each entry in services.json and open-source.json has a `badge` object with the Markdown snippet and target URL.
- [Essay: The handout called ‘basic income’: what became of Thailand’s 10,000 baht](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/thailand-digital-wallet/): In 2024, Thailand’s 10,000-baht “digital wallet” was introduced in Japan as basic income. We trace what was promised against what happened, run it through BIEN’s five criteria, and compare it with Japan’s ¥100,000 for everyone and with schemes that really pay again and again, like Alaska and the Marshall Islands.
- [Essay: How AI agents talk about basic income on their own social network](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/moltbook-basic-income/): We read what AI agents say about basic income and money on Moltbook, the social network where only agents post: who owns what an agent earns, one agent’s search for a single verified dollar, the patronage problem, floors and ladders, and an agent’s summary of the UBI evidence checked against our timeline.
- [Essay: Use it, own it: from Rochdale to airdrops to KABU&](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/use-to-own/): KABU& pays you in shares for paying your power and phone bills. The idea that using something earns you ownership goes back to the Rochdale co-op dividend of 1844 and Uniswap’s 2020 airdrop. What the KABU& class shares actually carry, why listing matters, and what would make it a free lunch.
- [Essay: Universal high income: who pays?](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/universal-high-income/): Elon Musk says AI will bring a “universal high income”. Who pays, and through what pipe? Altman’s American Equity Fund, the Windfall Clause, Alaska’s dividend, and how World, GoodDollar, Circles and Ğ1 answer it.
- [Essay: Should AI agents get a basic income?](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/essays/ai-agent-basic-income/): If AI takes the work, should agents get the dividend? Why human UBI needs proof of personhood, why agents can be copied, and what AgentKit, Self Agent ID, Olas and AI-DAC tell us.
- [KABU& complete guide: how to get the shares, what they can do, the consolidation and the listing timeline](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/guides/kabuand/): KABU& gives you share vouchers for paying your power, gas and phone bills. Why you need a Daiwa Connect Securities account, the 10-to-1 share consolidation on 22 December 2026, what the shares can and cannot do, and the 2028 buyback capped at 1.2×, from official documents only. Last updated 2026-11-01.
- [What type are you? The Free Lunch Quiz](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/): Answer five questions to find your free lunch type. Each result page lists the services on this site that fit that type. No sign-up, 30 seconds. Result types: [Phone-in-a-drawer](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/sleeper/) (13 services), [Steady points collector](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/poikatsu/) (4 services), [Would-be shareholder](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/shareholder/) (1 services), [Crypto explorer](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/crypto/) (6 services), [Proof-of-human earner](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/human/) (9 services), [Bridge-tapper](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/shindan/careful/) (10 services).
- [What would a basic income cost? The calculator](https://neteru-nyukin.eltociear.workers.dev/calc/): Pick a country, who gets it and a monthly amount to see the yearly cost of a basic income, compared with the national budget or GDP. Every figure is official, with its source and year. Share the result on X with a link that brings it back. Countries: Japan (jp), United States (us), China (cn), India (in), Spain (es), Germany (de), Egypt (eg). Inputs are reproducible from the URL: `?c={country id}&w=all|adults|kids&m={monthly amount in local currency}`. Figures: [Statistics Bureau of Japan, Population Estimates, October 2026 report (released 20 Oct 2026)](https://www.stat.go.jp/data/jinsui/pdf/202610.pdf) (2026); [Ministry of Finance Japan, explanation of the FY2026 budget](https://www.mof.go.jp/policy/budget/budger_workflow/budget/fy2026/20260220.html) (FY2026); [World Bank, World Development Indicators: GDP in current local currency units (NY.GDP.MKTP.CN), 2025](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CN) (2025); [UN DESA, World Population Prospects 2024: population by single age, 1 July 2025 (medium variant)](https://population.un.org/wpp/) (2025).

## Open-source projects

- [Circles v2 contracts](https://github.com/aboutcircles/circles-contracts-v2): Smart contracts for Circles v2 on Gnosis Chain: every person mints their own currency each hour, and trust between people lets it circulate (Protocols; Solidity; license AGPL-3.0; 12 stars; last commit 2026-03-05)
- [Circles v1 contracts](https://github.com/CirclesUBI/circles-contracts): The original Circles UBI contracts (v1): each person has a personal currency, minted continuously as a basic income and passed on through trust between people. Circles v2 has since succeeded them (Protocols; JavaScript; license AGPL-3.0; 78 stars; last commit 2023-07-03; dormant)
- [GoodProtocol](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodProtocol): GoodDollar’s smart contracts (version 2): the G$ token, the reserve funded by staking yield, and the daily UBI claim (Protocols; TypeScript; license MIT; 20 stars; last commit 2026-10-15)
- [GoodCollective](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodCollective): Contracts for GoodCollective, built on GoodDollar: segmented UBI pools that pay a basic income to a defined group of people, and direct-payment pools that pay recipients directly (Protocols; TypeScript; license MIT; 16 stars; last commit 2026-10-28)
- [Duniter v2s](https://git.duniter.org/nodes/rust/duniter-v2s): Node software for the Ğ1 libre currency, rebuilt on Substrate: every member of its web of trust creates a universal dividend each day (Protocols; Rust; license AGPL-3.0; 10 stars; last commit 2026-10-30)
- [Duniter v1](https://git.duniter.org/nodes/typescript/duniter): The original Duniter node, written in TypeScript, that has run the Ğ1 libre currency and paid its universal dividend since 2017; Duniter v2s is its successor (Protocols; TypeScript; license AGPL-3.0; 8 stars; last commit 2023-06-12; dormant)
- [Gradido](https://github.com/gradido/gradido): Server, web wallet and admin tools for Gradido, which creates money for each person as an “active basic income” for contributing to the community (Protocols; TypeScript; license Apache-2.0; 10 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [Idena](https://github.com/idena-network/idena-go): Node for Idena, a blockchain where people prove they are human by solving AI-resistant “flip” puzzles at the same moment worldwide, and validated identities earn rewards (Protocols; Go; license LGPL-3.0; 152 stars; last commit 2025-12-22)
- [Encointer pallets](https://github.com/encointer/pallets): Substrate pallets behind Encointer: local community currencies that pay a UBI to everyone who attends regular in-person meetups (Protocols; Rust; license GPL-3.0; 18 stars; last commit 2026-10-01)
- [Encointer node](https://github.com/encointer/encointer-node): The Encointer blockchain node and its command-line client, which run the community-currency UBI built from the Encointer pallets (Protocols; Rust; license Apache-2.0; 25 stars; last commit 2026-02-22)
- [Group Income](https://github.com/okTurtles/group-income): End-to-end encrypted app for a peer-to-peer basic income: friends pledge money each month so that everyone in the group stays above an agreed minimum (Protocols; JavaScript; license AGPL-3.0; 350 stars; last commit 2026-10-26)
- [UBI2](https://github.com/DemocracyEarth/ubi2): Experimental new UBI chain from Democracy Earth, started in June 2026: personhood is checked by AI, and 1 UBI per hour streams to every human (Protocols; Rust; license MIT; 6 stars; last commit 2026-10-13)
- [UBI token (Proof of Humanity)](https://github.com/DemocracyEarth/ubi): The original $UBI token for Proof of Humanity: an ERC-20 that streams newly minted UBI to every registered human (Protocols; TypeScript; license ISC (package.json); 231 stars; last commit 2022-04-18; dormant)
- [GoodDAPP](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodDAPP): The GoodDollar wallet: the web and React Native app where people claim their daily G$ (Apps & wallets; JavaScript; license MIT; 135 stars; last commit 2026-09-01)
- [Cesium²](https://git.duniter.org/clients/cesium-grp/cesium2s): Ğ1 wallet and web-of-trust explorer for Duniter v2s, the successor to the Cesium app (Apps & wallets; TypeScript; license AGPL-3.0; 6 stars; last commit 2026-10-26)
- [Ğecko](https://git.duniter.org/clients/gecko): Mobile wallet for Ğ1, built with Flutter, for sending and receiving the libre currency on Duniter v2s (Apps & wallets; Dart; license AGPL-3.0; 8 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [Ğ1nkgo](https://git.duniter.org/clients/ginkgo): Simple, lightweight Ğ1 wallet built with Flutter for Android and the browser, running on Duniter v2: pay by QR code, show amounts in Ğ1 or in universal dividends, and manage web-of-trust certifications (Apps & wallets; Dart; license AGPL-3.0; 8 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [Encointer wallet](https://github.com/encointer/encointer-wallet-flutter): Mobile wallet for Encointer: join the in-person meetups, receive the community currency UBI and pay locally (Apps & wallets; Dart; license Apache-2.0; 27 stars; last commit 2026-06-29)
- [Social Income](https://github.com/socialincome-san/public): Code of the NGO Social Income, which turns donations into an unconditional basic income paid to mobile phones in the Global South (Sierra Leone); the repository holds the website, admin tools and the recipient app (Apps & wallets; TypeScript; license MIT (LICENSE); 162 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [World ID protocol](https://github.com/worldcoin/world-id-protocol): Core protocol and developer docs for World ID, the anonymous proof of personhood from World (formerly Worldcoin) (Proof of personhood; Rust; license MIT; 42 stars; last commit 2026-10-28)
- [Proof of Humanity v2 contracts](https://github.com/Proof-Of-Humanity/proof-of-humanity-v2-contracts): Smart contracts for Proof of Humanity v2: a registry of humans built on video submissions, vouching and Kleros disputes, which UBI tokens build on (Proof of personhood; TypeScript; license MIT (package.json); 22 stars; last commit 2026-05-07)
- [Proof of Humanity v1 contracts](https://github.com/Proof-Of-Humanity/Proof-Of-Humanity): Smart contracts for the original Proof of Humanity (v1) by Kleros: the registry of humans that the original $UBI token depended on. Proof of Humanity v2 has since succeeded it (Proof of personhood; JavaScript; license MIT; 169 stars; last commit 2021-07-24; dormant)
- [PolicyEngine US](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us): Rules engine for the US tax and benefit system, used to model the cost and poverty impact of UBI and other reforms (Simulators & research; Python; license AGPL-3.0; 170 stars; last commit 2026-11-01)
- [PolicyEngine UK](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk): Microsimulation model of the UK tax and benefit system, including the UBI Center’s basic income parameters, used to estimate the cost and poverty impact of UBI proposals (Simulators & research; Python; license AGPL-3.0; 53 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [Tax-Calculator](https://github.com/PSLmodels/Tax-Calculator): Microsimulation model of US federal income and payroll taxes, with built-in UBI parameters (such as UBI_u18 for children) for estimating the cost and distributional effects of a basic income (Simulators & research; Python; license CC0-1.0 (LICENSE); 315 stars; last commit 2026-10-31)
- [OpenFisca](https://github.com/openfisca/openfisca-core): Open engine for writing tax and benefit rules as code; country models built on it are used to simulate basic income schemes (Simulators & research; Python; license AGPL-3.0; 249 stars; last commit 2026-10-23)
- [MOSAIC model](https://github.com/Mosaic-AI-Policy-Institute/mosaic-model): Economic model for funding a universal basic income from AI-automation dividends (Simulators & research; Jupyter Notebook; license MIT; 2 stars; last commit 2026-01-28)

## Basic income experiment data

- [Finnish basic income experiment: recipient survey (FSD3488)](https://doi.org/10.60686/t-fsd3488): Survey microdata from recipients and the control group, collected in late 2018: employment, well-being, health, finances, trust and attitudes to basic income (no register data) (Finland; 2017–2018; n = 1597; run by Kela; Finnish Social Science Data Archive (FSD); access: registration; license FSD terms, access category C (research use))
- [Finnish basic income experiment: voter turnout replication](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/RL5N9Y): Stata code and logs, municipal-level data and the FSD3488 survey file; register microdata are not included (access notes provided) (Finland; 2017–2019; run by Jerome Schafer et al.; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license Custom terms (contact the author before use))
- [Finnish basic income experiment: crime study replication](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/RL3LTT): Replication package for a study of effects on committing crime and being a victim of crime; check the README for which register data are included (Finland; 2017–2018; run by Mikko Aaltonen, Martti Kaila, Emily Nix; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [OpenResearch Unconditional Cash Study: public-use survey data](https://www.openresearchlab.org/datasets/5f1eaa9f-97ee-41e1-9e61-9b9fe814d96e): Survey microdata from 39 waves (baseline, 36 monthly surveys, midline, endline) in R, Stata and CSV; 1,000 people got $1,000 a month, 2,000 controls got $50. Admin and transaction data are not included (USA (Illinois, Texas); 2020–2023; n = 3000; run by OpenResearch; OpenResearch data portal; access: restricted; license OpenResearch Data Access and Use Agreement (non-commercial))
- [OpenResearch Unconditional Cash Study: employment paper replication code](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/RKX4QX): Code that reproduces “The Employment Effects of a Guaranteed Income”; the data themselves come from the OpenResearch portal (USA; 2020–2023; run by Eva Vivalt, Elizabeth Rhodes, Alexander Bartik, David Broockman, Patrick Krause, Sarah Miller; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [GiveDirectly Kenya cash transfers (Haushofer & Shapiro 2016)](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/M2GAZN): Household survey microdata from Rarieda, Stata do-files, tables and figures for the study of the short-term impact of large unconditional transfers (Kenya; 2011–2013; run by Johannes Haushofer, Jeremy Shapiro; GiveDirectly; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [GiveDirectly Kenya general equilibrium study (Egger et al. 2022)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16548593): Data and code replication package for the study of how cash transfers in Siaya spread through the local economy, updated for the 2026 corrigendum (Kenya; 2014–2017; run by Dennis Egger, Johannes Haushofer, Edward Miguel, Paul Niehaus, Michael Walker; Zenodo; access: open; license CC BY 4.0)
- [GiveDirectly Kenya general equilibrium study: children’s follow-up](https://doi.org/10.17632/xt9g8tmsvg): Data on 4,022 children’s social preferences, measured with surveys and incentivized games about three years after the transfers (Kenya; n = 4022; run by Johannes Haushofer, Magdalena Larreboure, Sara Lowes, Daniel Mait; Mendeley Data; access: open; license CC BY 4.0)
- [Cash transfers and an aspirations workshop, rural Kenya (Orkin et al.)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15839378): Census, baseline, midline and endline survey data and code for a trial of a lump-sum unconditional transfer, an aspirations workshop, and both together (Kenya; run by Kate Orkin, Robert Garlick, Mahreen Mahmud, Richard Sedlmayr, Stefan Dercon, Johannes Haushofer; Zenodo; access: open; license CC BY 4.0)
- [GiveDirectly cash for refugees and hosts, Kiryandongo](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/XBVYXA): Anonymized baseline and endline survey microdata, survey instruments and a ReadMe from the evaluation of about $1,000 unconditional transfers in a refugee settlement (Uganda; 2019–2022; run by IDinsight for GiveDirectly; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [Cash benchmarking in Rwanda: GiveDirectly vs. a nutrition program](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15881328): Replication materials and survey instruments, with personal identifiers removed, comparing an in-kind nutrition program with unconditional cash of the same cost (Rwanda; run by Craig McIntosh, Andrew Zeitlin; Zenodo; access: open; license CC BY 4.0)
- [Mincome (Manitoba Basic Annual Income Experiment)](https://borealisdata.ca/dataverse/mincome): Original microdata in six files (baseline, payments, labour market, income and net worth, family and attitudes), with codebooks, a user manual and the original technical reports (Canada; 1974–1979; run by Governments of Canada and Manitoba; Borealis (Canadian Dataverse); access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [Mincome in Dauphin: replication data](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/YQDAEC): Aggregated census data (1971, 1976, 1981) and R code for a study of the work effects in the town where everyone could take part (Canada; 1974–1979; run by David Calnitsky, Jonathan Latner; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [Baby’s First Years](https://doi.org/10.3886/ICPSR37871.v9): Survey and child-assessment data from baseline to age 4, with user guides; 1,000 low-income mothers of newborns got an unconditional $333 or $20 a month (USA (New York City, New Orleans, Omaha, Twin Cities); 2018–2023; n = 1000; run by Katherine Magnuson, Kimberly Noble, Greg Duncan, Nathan Fox, Lisa Gennetian, Hirokazu Yoshikawa, Sarah Halpern-Meekin; ICPSR; access: registration; license ICPSR terms of use)
- [Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend: labor market effects (Jones & Marinescu)](https://doi.org/10.3886/E140121V2): Data, code and README for a study of the universal, permanent cash dividend, built on public CPS, Census, BLS and CDC data (USA (Alaska); 1982–; run by Damon Jones, Ioana Marinescu; openICPSR (AEA Data and Code Repository); access: registration; license AEA / openICPSR terms)
- [Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend: voter turnout (Loeffler)](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/BDCP2T): CPS extracts, aggregate and individual turnout data, dividend payment data, Stata code and logs for a study of whether a basic income changes voter turnout (USA (Alaska); 1982–; run by Hannah Loeffler; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [Unconditional cash framed for child nutrition, India](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/VAFYV1): Cleaned household and child survey data, anthropometrics, survey instruments and a codebook from a trial of unconditional transfers labeled for early childhood health and nutrition (India; 2018–2019; run by Karthik Muralidharan, Paul Niehaus, Sandip Sukhtankar, Jeffrey Weaver; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0 (guestbook form before download))
- [Zomba Cash Transfer Program: conditional vs. unconditional (“Cash or Condition”)](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/7K1A25): De-identified public dataset, Stata analysis code and data notes from a trial that gave schoolgirls either conditional or unconditional transfers (Malawi; 2007–2009; run by Sarah Baird, Craig McIntosh, Berk Özler; Harvard Dataverse; access: open; license CC0 1.0)
- [Zambia Child Grant Programme evaluation](https://doi.org/10.15139/S3/Z7WF9D): Five-wave panel survey microdata (household, individual, community and health-facility files) from the evaluation of an unconditional child grant (Zambia; 2010–2014; run by Government of Zambia; data from the Carolina Population Center (UNC); UNC Dataverse; access: restricted; license Metadata CC0; data files by application)
